al_freebird_buttress.blurb: A small buttress in the Northeast Section of Buck's Pocket, in Jackson County, Alabama. It has nine routes, seven sport and two trad, with a wide spread from 5.9 up to the mid-5.13 range. Three routes sit at 5.9, three at 5.12, and the rest are scattered between, so there is something for moderate and hard sport climbers alike, though not much at the easy end. Reaching it takes a trail walk of roughly twenty minutes from the roadside pull-out for the northern part of the park, and the crag is still lightly documented.

al_creekside.blurb: A fairly large group of boulders beside South Sauty Creek at Buck's Pocket, in northeast Alabama. It has nine problems, all bouldering, and the grades split into two camps: a few easy V0 to V1 lines plus mid-range V4 and V5, then a hard cluster between V8 and V9. The approach is short, five to seven minutes along the main ATV trail with the boulders on your right. The park around it is remote and quiet, tucked into the folds of Sand Mountain, so expect a peaceful session rather than a crowded one.

al_ninja_camp_boulders.blurb: A hard-leaning bouldering area in the Citadel near Fort Payne, Alabama. It has nine problems, none easy: the grades start at V6 and run through V7 and V10 to a single V13 at the top end. It is a fit for sloper enthusiasts, with plenty of sloping holds, and the main line is named as one of the field's test pieces. The boulders lie a few minutes down the trail beyond the Snail, so the walk is short. The sandstone of the wider Citadel brings roofs, sloper top-outs and technical faces.
